extracted.intended_audience: operators of onshore hazardous liquid and carbon dioxide pipelines; pipeline safety/compliance personnel; PHMSA reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of regulatory requirements in 49 CFR part 195 related to valve installation, capabilities, monitoring, maintenance, notifications, and integrity-management devices (RMVs, ASVs, RCVs, EFRDs) for onshore hazardous liquid and CO2 pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to notify PHMSA (§195.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: An operator must provide any notification required by this part by: (1) sending by electronic mail to InformationResourcesManager@dot.gov; or (2) sending by mail to ATTN: Information Resources Manager, DOT/PHMSA/OPS, East Building, 2nd Floor, E22-321, 1200 New Jersey Ave. SE, Washington, DC 20590. An operator must also notify the appropriate State or local pipeline safety authority when an applicable pipeline segment is located in a State where OPS has an interstate agent agreement, or an intrastate pipeline segment is regulated by that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise specified, notifications requesting use of a different integrity assessment method, analytical method, sampling approach, compliance timeline, or technique (e.g., 'other technology' or 'alternative equivalent technology') must be submitted to PHMSA at least 90 days in advance. An operator may proceed to use the other method 91 days after submittal unless PHMSA objects or requests more time/information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for certain steel pipeline work (post-July 3, 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: For steel pipelines contracted, replaced, relocated, or otherwise changed after July 3, 2009: (i) design/install/construct/initially inspect/test in compliance with this part unless converted under §195.5; (ii) except for pipelines subject to §195.260(e), such pipelines are not subject to the RMV and alternative equivalent technology requirements in §§195.258(c) and (d), 195.418, and 195.419.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits RMV applicability for certain steel pipeline changes after the 2009 date, except where §195.260(e) applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: RMV or alternative technology installation for new/entirely replaced pipelines (§195.258(c),(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: For all onshore hazardous liquid or carbon dioxide pipeline segments with diameters ≥6 inches constructed after April 10, 2023, or entirely replaced after that date, the operator must install rupture-mitigation valves (RMV) or an alternative equivalent technology whenever a valve must be installed to meet the appropriate valve spacing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An operator using alternative equivalent technology must notify PHMSA per §195.18. All installed RMVs and alternative equivalent technology must meet §195.419. Operators may request extensions of installation compliance deadlines if they can demonstrate economic, technical, or operational infeasibility to PHMSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of notification for alternative equivalent technology (§195.258(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an operator elects to use alternative equivalent technology, the operator must notify PHMSA per §195.18 and include a technical and safety evaluation in its notice. Valves installed as alternative equivalent technology must comply with §§195.418, 195.419, and 195.420.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An operator requesting use of manual valves must include a demonstration that installing an RMV would be economically, technically, or operationally infeasible. A manual compressor station valve at a continuously manned station may be used as alternative equivalent technology and would not require a §195.18 notification, but it must comply with §§195.419 and 195.420.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve locations — general list (§195.260)
rubrics_metrics.description: A valve must be installed at: (a) suction and discharge ends of a pump station to permit isolation in an emergency; (b) each pipeline entering or leaving a breakout storage tank area to permit tank isolation; (c) locations along the system that will minimize or prevent safety risks, property damage, or environmental harm, as appropriate for onshore/offshore/HCAs; (d) each lateral takeoff to permit shutting off the lateral without interrupting flow; (e) each side of adjacent water crossings >100 ft wide with flood/equipment protections; (f) each side of a reservoir holding water for human consumption; (g) on each HVL pipeline in high-population/other populated areas built or where ≥2 miles replaced within 5 contiguous miles after April 10, 2023 (with maximum spacing rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For newly constructed or entirely replaced onshore segments installed after April 10, 2023, valve spacing must not exceed 15 miles for segments that could affect or are in HCAs and 20 miles for segments that could not affect HCAs. Valves on segments in or affecting HCAs must be installed as determined by the operator's preventive/mitigative measure process but with maximum distance not exceeding 7.5 miles from HCA endpoints. Operators may request site-specific exemptions or extensions per §195.18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve spacing for HCA and non-HCA segments (§195.260(c) & (g))
rubrics_metrics.description: For newly constructed or entirely replaced onshore segments installed after April 10, 2023: valve spacing must not exceed 15 miles for segments that could affect or are in HCAs, and 20 miles for segments that could not affect HCAs. Valves in HCAs or which could affect HCAs must be installed as determined by the operator's process, but with a maximum distance not to exceed 7½ miles from HCA endpoints. For HVL pipelines in populated areas the max spacing is 7½ miles, which may be increased by 1.25× (up to 9 3/8 miles) with PHMSA review and recordkeeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators may request an exemption from compliance deadlines if they demonstrate infeasibility per §195.18. For increased HVL spacing, operator must notify PHMSA and retain supporting records for the pipeline's useful life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions and extensions for valve installation/spacing (§195.260(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: An operator may submit for PHMSA review a notification requesting site-specific exemption from valve installation or spacing requirements of paragraphs (c), (e), or (f), demonstrating the exemption would not adversely affect safety. An operator may also request an extension of compliance deadlines because meeting them would be economically, technically, or operationally infeasible for a particular project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications and demonstrations must follow §195.18 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural manual: identification of immediate-response facilities and valves (§195.402(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators' procedural manuals must include determining which pipeline facilities are in areas requiring an immediate response to prevent hazards to the public, property, or the environment if facilities failed, including segments that could affect HCAs or are in HCAs, and valves specified in §195.418 or §195.452(i)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This determination informs emergency response and preventive planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural manual: accident/failure investigation and analysis (§195.402(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must investigate and analyze pipeline accidents and failures, including sending failed pipe, component, or equipment for laboratory testing or examination where appropriate, to determine causes and contributing factors and to minimize recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must incorporate findings into prevention and response practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-failure lessons learned and incorporation (§195.402(i)(post-failure))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each operator must develop, implement, and incorporate lessons learned from a post-failure and accident review into written procedures, including relevant personnel training and qualifications programs, and in design, construction, testing, maintenance, operations, and emergency procedure manuals and specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessons learned should result in tangible updates across programs and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-failure analysis of RMV/alternative closure factors (§195.402(i)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a failure involves closure of an RMV or alternative equivalent technology, the operator must conduct a post-failure analysis of all factors that may have impacted release volume and consequences and identify/implement O&M measures to minimize future consequences. The analysis must include detection/identification/operational response/communications; appropriateness/effectiveness of procedures and systems (SCADA, communications, valve shut-off, personnel); actual response time from rupture identification to mitigation; location and timeliness of RMV or alternative actuation; and any other factors the operator deems appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis must be comprehensive and lead to corrective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-failure summary, timing, review, and record retention (§195.402(i)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a failure involves identification of a rupture or RMV/alternative closure, the operator must complete a summary of the post-failure review within 90 days. While the investigation is pending, the operator must conduct quarterly status reviews until completion. The final summary and all related reviews/analyses must be reviewed, dated, and signed by the appropriate senior executive officer. Operators must keep the final summary, investigation documents, and lessons-learned records for the useful life of the pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly status reviews continue until finalization; retention is for useful life of pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications with public safety answering points and emergency agencies (§195.402(c)(12), (e)(1),(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must establish and maintain adequate means of communication with the appropriate public safety answering point (9-1-1), where direct access exists, and fire, police, and other public officials. Operators must determine responsibilities, resources, jurisdictions, and emergency contact numbers for all responding government organizations and inform them about the operator's ability to respond and means of communication. Operators may establish liaison with local emergency coordinating agencies in lieu of communicating individually with each entity. The operator must immediately and directly notify the appropriate 9-1-1 or coordinating agency after notification of potential rupture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing liaisons can substitute for many individual contacts; immediate notification to 9-1-1 is required after a notification of potential rupture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and thresholds for 'notification of potential rupture' (§195.417)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notification of potential rupture means notification to or observation by an operator of indicia of a potential unintentional or uncontrolled large-volume release, including: (1) an unanticipated/unexplained pressure loss outside normal operating pressures (established as >10% loss within 15 minutes unless operator documents a different threshold due to flow dynamics); (2) an unanticipated/unexplained flow rate/pressure/equipment/instrument indication at upstream or downstream stations representative of (1); or (3) any unanticipated/unexplained rapid release of a large volume, a fire, or an explosion in the immediate vicinity of the pipeline. A notification occurs when an operator first receives notice of or observes such an event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must set in written procedures what constitutes 'normal operating pressures' and may document different pressure-change thresholds if operationally justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and operational timeline for RMVs (§195.418(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: For newly constructed and entirely replaced onshore hazardous liquid or carbon dioxide pipeline segments ≥6 inches that could affect HCAs or are located in HCAs and installed after April 10, 2023, operators must install or use existing RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies according to this section and §195.419. RMVs and alternatives must be operational within 14 days of placing the segment in service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators may request an extension of the 14-day operation requirement if they demonstrate infeasibility per §195.18. Requirements apply to all applicable pipe replacements, even if replacement does not directly involve valve addition/replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shut-off segment definition and minimum valve requirement (§195.418(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'shut-off segment' is the pipeline between the upstream valve closest to the upstream endpoint of the replaced pipeline segment in the HCA (or segment that could affect an HCA) and the downstream valve closest to the downstream endpoint, such that the entirety of the segment that could affect the HCA or the segment within the HCA is between at least two RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies. All entirely replaced onshore segments that could affect or are in an HCA must include a minimum of one valve that meets this section and §195.419.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If crossover or lateral pipes connect between upstream and downstream valves, the shut-off segment extends to valves on those connections so that closing all valves leaves no flow path to the rupture site except residual liquids.

rubrics_metrics.name: RMV shut-off segment valve spacing and laterals (§195.418(b)(2)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: RMVs/alternatives protecting shut-off segments must not exceed: (i) for non-HVL segments: 15 miles, with a maximum distance not exceeding 7½ miles from the endpoints of a shut-off segment; (ii) for HVL segments: 7½ miles. Maximum intervals for these valves may be increased by 1.25× up to 9 3/8 miles at an endpoint with notification per §195.260(g). Laterals contributing <5% of total shut-off segment volume may have RMVs/alternatives located elsewhere if all such laterals together contribute ≤5% of segment volume; check valves may be used as alternatives where positioned to stop flow into the lateral (check valves not subject to §195.419 but must follow §195.420).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators using such alternatives must submit requests per §195.18; laterals' volume contribution is based on maximum flow at operating pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crossovers and manual valve alternative requirements (§195.418(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: An operator may use a manual valve as an alternative equivalent technology for a crossover connection if, during normal operations, the valve is closed to prevent flow with a locking device or other means preventing opening by unauthorized persons. The operator must document that the valve has been closed and locked per the operator's lock-out/tag-out procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators using such a manual valve as an alternative must submit a request to PHMSA per §195.18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual operation procedures and response time considerations (§195.418(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators using a manual valve as an alternative must develop and implement operating procedures and appropriately designate and locate nearby personnel to ensure valve shut-off per this section and §195.419. Manual operation must include time for assembling personnel, acquiring tools/equipment, driving under heavy traffic at posted speed limits, walking to the valve, and time to manually shut off all valves, and must not exceed the response time in §195.419(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The operator's planning must realistically account for all time components to meet the 30-minute requirement (or other applicable requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rupture identification and valve shut-off time (§195.419(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an operator observes or is notified of a release that may be representative of an unintentional or uncontrolled release (per §§195.2 and 195.417), the operator must, as soon as practicable but within 30 minutes of rupture identification (§195.402(e)(4)), identify the rupture and fully close any RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies necessary to minimize released volume and mitigate consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 30-minute window is measured from rupture identification, and operators must ensure procedures and capabilities meet this timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve actuation and monitoring capabilities (§195.419(c)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A valve must have the actuation capability necessary to close an RMV or alternative equivalent technology to mitigate rupture consequences. RMVs/alternatives must be capable of being monitored or controlled by remote or onsite personnel, operated during normal/abnormal/emergency conditions, monitored for valve status (open/closed/partial), upstream pressure, and downstream pressure. For ASVs, remote status monitoring is not required if the operator can monitor pressures or flow rates on each segment to identify/locate a rupture. Backup power is required to maintain SCADA or other remote communications or valves must be monitored/controlled on-site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring of RMV position/status must be via electronic communication with remote instrumentation or equivalent means; ASV monitoring exceptions exist when segment pressures/flow are monitored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow modeling and ASV use as RMV (§195.419(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to using an ASV as an RMV, the operator must conduct flow modeling for the shut-off segment and any laterals so the valve will close within 30 minutes or less following rupture identification, consistent with operator procedures. The modeling must include anticipated maximum/normal/other flow volumes, pressures, or operating conditions for a period not to exceed 15 months and must cover flow between RMVs/alternatives and any looped pipelines or receipt tie-ins. If operating conditions change in ways that affect ASV set pressures or the 30-minute closure time, a new flow model and ASV reset are required prior to the next review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow modeling must include a time/pressure chart for the segment containing the ASV and be conducted prior to making flow condition changes that could render the 30-minute closure unachievable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption request for manual valves on non-HCA segments (§195.419(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: For pipeline segments not in an HCA or that could not affect an HCA, an operator submitting a notification for use of manual valves as an alternative may also request an exemption from the valve operation requirements of §195.419(b) (the 30-minute requirement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption requests follow §195.18 procedures and require justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve inspection frequency and partial-operation requirement (§195.420(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each operator must, at least twice each calendar year, but at intervals not exceeding 7½ months, inspect each valve to determine that it is functioning properly. Each RMV or alternative equivalent technology installed under §195.258(c) or §195.418 must also be partially operated. Operators are not required to close the valve fully during the drill; a minimum 25 percent valve closure is sufficient unless operational information requires a greater closure percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspections must demonstrate functioning; partial operation at minimum 25% is acceptable for demonstrating reliability unless additional closure is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-to-point verification for RCVs (§195.420(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each remote-control valve (RCV) installed under §195.258(c) or §195.418, an operator must conduct a point-to-point verification between SCADA system displays and the installed valves, sensors, and communications equipment, per §195.446(c) and (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification ensures that SCADA indications correspond to physical valve and sensor states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drill and validation requirements for manually or locally operated alternatives (§195.420(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each alternative equivalent technology that is manually or locally operated (not an RMV), operators must achieve a 30-minute-or-less response time through an initial drill and periodic validation. Operators must review each phase of the drill and document results to validate total response time including rupture identification and valve shut-off. Operators must randomly select an authorized alternative for an annual 30-minute validation drill simulating worst-case conditions within each pipeline system and operating/maintenance field work unit. The drill must occur at least once each calendar year at intervals not to exceed 15 months. Minimum 25% valve closure is sufficient unless operational info requires more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must include in written procedures the random selection method. If the 30-minute time cannot be achieved in the drill, the operator must revise response efforts to achieve compliance no later than 12 months after the drill, and alternative shut-off measures must be in place within 7 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of lessons learned from drills (§195.420(e)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on response-time drill results, the operator must include lessons learned in: (i) training and qualifications programs; (ii) design, construction, testing, maintenance, operating, and emergency procedure manuals; and (iii) any other areas identified as needing improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drill outcomes must directly inform improvements in procedures and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial measures for inoperable valves (§195.420(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: For any valve installed under §195.258(c) or §195.418 or an RMV/alternative installed under §195.418 that is indicated to be inoperable or unable to maintain effective shut-off, the operator must: (1) repair or replace the valve as soon as practicable but no later than 12 months after finding it inoperable (extensions possible if infeasible); and (2) designate an alternative compliant valve within 7 calendar days of the finding while repairs are made and document an interim response plan to maintain safety. Alternative compliant valves are not required to comply with spacing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators may request compliance deadline extensions per §195.18 if repairing/replacing within 12 months is infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASV shut-in pressure confirmation timing (§195.420(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: An operator using an ASV as an RMV must document and confirm ASV shut-in pressures on a calendar year basis not to exceed 15 months. ASV shut-in set pressures must be proven and reset individually at each ASV at least each calendar year, but at intervals not to exceed 15 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties with flow modeling (§195.419(f)) and periodic review/reset requirements to maintain the 30-minute closure capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFRD determination, factors, and installation requirements (§195.452(i)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an operator determines that an Emergency Flow Restricting Device (EFRD) is needed on a pipeline segment located in or which could affect an HCA, the operator must install the EFRD. In making this determination, the operator must evaluate at least: swiftness of leak detection and pipeline shutdown capabilities; type of commodity; rate of potential leakage; volume that can be released; topography/pipeline profile; potential for ignition; proximity to power sources; location of nearest response personnel; specific terrain within the HCA or between the segment and the HCA; and benefits expected by reducing spill size. An RMV installed under this paragraph must meet all other applicable requirements in this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where EFRDs are installed on HCA segments ≥6 inches placed into service or where ≥2 miles replaced within 5 contiguous miles after April 10, 2023, their location/installation/actuation/operation/maintenance (including actuators, personnel response, control centers, SCADA, communications, and procedures) must meet the design/operation/testing/maintenance/rupture-mitigation requirements of §§195.258, 195.260, 195.402, 195.418, 195.419, and 195.420. EFRD analyses must be completed prior to placing such pipelines in service, and implementation of EFRD findings for RMVs must meet §195.418. Operators may request exemptions from compliance deadlines per §195.18 if infeasible.
